rows.ARS:
Medium yellow Hybrid Tea.
Registration name: MACwairar
Exhibition name: Aperitif ® (hybrid tea, McGredy 1988)
rows.Origin:
Bred by Samuel Darragh (1932-2019) McGredy IV (1988).
Introduced in New Zealand by McGredy Roses International (New Zealand) in 1998 as 'Aperitif'.
Introduced in United States by Jackson & Perkins (Wholesale) in 2001 as 'Aperitif'.
rows.Class: Hybrid Tea. (Series: New Generation Roses ® Collection)
rows.Bloom: Yellow. Mild, spice fragrance. Average diameter 4". Double (17-25 petals), borne mostly solitary, high-centered bloom form. Blooms in flushes throughout the season. Pointed, ovoid buds.
rows.Habit:
Bushy, upright. Large, matte, light green foliage.

Height: 43" to 6'1" (110 to 185cm).
rows.Growing: USDA zone 5b and warmer. Can be used for cut flower or garden. Vigorous. can be trained as a climber. Disease susceptibility: very disease resistant. Spring Pruning: Remove old canes and dead or diseased wood and cut back canes that cross. In warmer climates, cut back the remaining canes by about one-third. In colder areas, you'll probably find you'll have to prune a little more than that. Requires spring freeze protection (see glossary - Spring freeze protection) .
rows.Notes: Ludwigs Roses says this rose is a Climber. It produces clear, almost unfading yellow blooms of an impeccable Hybrid Tea shape...
